documents.title: Lease contract
documents.why: The increase can take effect only from the next termination date; the lease records the termination dates (and any graduated-rent or index clause, arts. 269b–269c).

must_show: date from which the increase applies
whether the form approved by the canton is used
documents.title: Landlord's rent increase notice
documents.why: An increase is void without the prescribed form or without reasons; only the notice itself shows the form used and the reasons given.

must_show: how it was delivered (registered-mail tracking, envelope or acknowledgement)
documents.title: Proof of the date the notice was received
documents.why: The notice must reach the tenant at least ten days before the notice period begins; proof of the date of receipt shows whether it did (and fixes the start of the 30-day challenge period, art. 270b(1)).

must_show: share passed on to the rent
documents.title: Landlord's breakdown of the cost increases or additional services relied on
documents.why: A rent justified by cost increases or additional services is in general not unfair; the landlord's breakdown of those costs or works ordinarily shows whether the increase is so justified.

documents.title: Landlord's notice of termination or written threat of termination
documents.why: The increase is void if accompanied by a notice or a threat of termination; the notice or the letter containing the threat shows whether it accompanied the increase.

facts.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling (mould, damp, heating), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase?
Does the claim state that the landlord has communicated to the tenant an increase of the rent of the dwelling (whether or not on an official form)?
Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?
Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?
Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination or threatened to terminate the lease?

notes.text: No presumption: a fact the claim does not state stays unresolved. No public text cited in this rule set supports presuming an unstated fact absent or a defining event present.
